note: Range step 2: slides across the break, on a lip roll down and as a siren, then the same slide on "oo" from a staff, and again on a second staff a step higher so the break sits inside it. The old Stage choice set a key, so the higher slide is now a second staff, written in a key, not moves: it is the key that puts a tenor's break inside the slide. missing: a tool that draws a sung slide between two notes on an open vowel (lip-roll only asks for a lip roll).

exercise.title: Slides across the break
exercise.why: A slide passes through every pitch between two notes, so it carries your voice across the break with no step to jump over: first on a lip roll, which keeps the sound light, then on an open sound.

cells.text:
Press Start below to begin the lip roll: a tone slides from head voice down to chest voice, then you make the same slide on your own while the mic draws your line. Keep the buzz loose and quiet.
On the way down there is a place where your voice wants to flip: that is the break. Practice until the buzz stays even through it.

Press Start below to begin the lip roll: the tone now slides up and back down, so you cross the break twice in each round. Let the slide get lighter, not louder, as it climbs.
If the buzz stops at the break, start the next slide more quietly.

Press Start exercise below: the drone and the mic start together, and your pitch shows as a line on the staff. Slide from the low {{1}} up to {{5}} and back down, in one unbroken sound like the lip roll. Sing it on "oo".
_Don't reach for high notes: keep the slide quiet, and stop if your throat tightens._

Once your line climbs without a jump, press Play on the second staff below to start its drone. Then press Start microphone.
Slide from its low {{1}} up to {{5}} the same way. Its {{1}} is a step higher, so the break sits further inside the slide.
